newsitem.title: UK: GKN rallies further on Sinter Metals bid.
newsitem.headline: GKN rallies further on Sinter Metals bid.

text.p: Shares in British engineering and automotive group GKN Plc continued to rise on Wednesday after earlier news it was bidding for U.S. Sinter Metals, dealers said.
GKN shares were up 32 pence, or 3.51 percent, to 943p by 1410 GMT in volume of 1.3 million while the FTSE-100 index was 14.4 points, or 0.32 percent, lower at 4418.8.
"The stock was oversold and looking for an excuse to bounce back," said a marketmaker at a British bank.

Today's rally took GKN away from 13-month lows around 900p, a level that also provided support in mid-February. In the interim the stock had a closing high at 1170p several times last October, with an intraday high at 1186p.
GKN, which plans to buy Sinter Metals for $570 million in cash and already has 43 percent acceptances, said the acquisition would be earnings enhancing in the first 12 months.
The bid will offer Sinter shareholders $37 per share, compared with Tuesday's closing price of $27. Sinter shares were up $9.5 at $36.5 in New York.
GKN has long been the subject of speculation it might bid for British engineering firm Vickers Group Plc. The story resurfaced in last weekend's newspapers.
Vickers shares were 3p lower at 212p in turnover of 270,000.
